questions.question: A clock was set right at 6 AM on 1 January 2015. It loses 10 seconds every hour. What time (in AM) will the clock show on 2nd January 2015 at 6 AM?
questions.solution:
The clock was set correctly at **6 AM on 1 January 2015**.

We need to find the time shown at **6 AM on 2 January 2015**.

Total time duration elapsed = **24 hours**

Given that the clock loses **10 seconds every hour**:

Total loss in 24 hours = 24 × 10 = 240 seconds

Convert the total loss into minutes:

60 seconds = 1 minute

240 seconds = 240 ÷ 60 = **4 minutes**

The clock time is calculated by subtracting the loss from the actual time:

Time shown = **6:00 AM** − 4 minutes

Time shown = **5:56 AM**

Hence, the clock will show **5:56 AM** on 2nd January 2015.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: In which year did the IAAF change its name to World Athletics?

• This rebranding initiative was led by the organization’s President, **Sebastian Coe**, as part of a broader strategy to make the sport more **modern**, **accessible**, and **marketable** to a global audience.

• The **Bangkok Declaration** defined the group as a **bridge** between **South Asia** and **Southeast Asia**, emphasizing **technical and economic cooperation** among nations bordering the **Bay of Bengal**.

• The grouping expanded on **December 22, 1997**, when **Myanmar** became a full member, leading to the name change to **BIMST-EC**.
 
• With the admission of **Nepal** and **Bhutan** in **February 2004**, the organization was finally renamed the **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)**.

• The phrase was used to describe the **stagnant annual growth rate** of the **Indian economy**, which averaged around **3.5%** for several decades between the **1950s** and the **1980s**.
 
• During this period, despite various **Five-Year Plans**, the **per capita income** growth remained very low, averaging only about **1.3%** per annum due to high **population growth**.
 
• The term metaphorically suggested that the **slow pace of development** was a result of a **fatalistic** or **contented** cultural outlook, though it was actually a critique of the **restrictive economic policies** and the **License Raj**.

• A key architect of the **1991 Economic Reforms** in India.
 
• He served as the **Deputy Chairman** of the **Planning Commission** and was the first **Director** of the **Independent Evaluation Office** at the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**.
 
 
 
• **Jagdish Bhagwati**:
 
 
• An eminent **Professor of Economics** at **Columbia University** known for his advocacy of **free trade**.
 
• His work heavily influenced the transition of the Indian economy from **protectionism** to **globalization**.
 
 
 
• **Amartya Sen**:
 
 
• An **Indian economist** and **philosopher** who was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences** in **1998**.
 
• He is celebrated for his contributions to **welfare economics**, **social choice theory**, and his work on the causes of **famine** and **human development**.
 
 
 
• **License Raj**:
 
 
• Refers to the system of **elaborate licenses**, regulations, and **red tape** required to set up and run businesses in India between **1947** and **1990**.
 
• This system is widely cited as the primary reason for the **economic stagnation** associated with the **Hindu rate of growth**.

questions.question: Which index is used to measure headline inflation in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Consumer Price Index Combined**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Headline inflation** represents the total inflation in an economy, encompassing a wide basket of goods and services including volatile components like **food** and **fuel** prices.
 
• In **India**, the **Consumer Price Index (CPI) Combined** is currently utilized as the definitive measure for headline inflation. This shift was officially adopted by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **April 2014**.
 
• The adoption of **CPI Combined** (which includes both **rural** and **urban** data) followed the recommendations of the **Urjit Patel Committee**, which suggested moving away from the **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)** to better reflect the cost of living for citizens.
 
• The data for **CPI Combined** is released monthly by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• The index uses a base year of **2012** and is the primary anchor for the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** to maintain price stability with a target inflation rate of **4%** and a tolerance band of **plus/minus 2%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)**:

 
 
• It tracks the changes in the price of goods sold and traded in bulk by wholesale businesses.
 
• The index is published by the **Office of Economic Adviser**, **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**.
 
• Unlike **CPI**, it does not account for the prices of **services**, focusing solely on physical commodities.
 
 
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP) Deflator**:
 
 
• This is a comprehensive measure of inflation calculated as the ratio of **Nominal GDP** to **Real GDP** multiplied by 100.
 
• It covers all goods and services produced within the domestic economy, but it is typically available only on a **quarterly** or **annual** basis, unlike the monthly CPI.
 
 
 
• **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)**:
 
 
• It measures the growth in the volume of industrial production across sectors such as **Mining**, **Manufacturing**, and **Electricity**.
 
• It is an indicator of industrial activity and economic health rather than a direct measure of price inflation.

• The Sultan, impressed by his expertise in **Islamic Law**, appointed him as the **Qazi** (Judge) of **Delhi**, a post he held for approximately eight years.
 
• His famous travelogue, written in **Arabic** and titled **Rihla** (The Journey), provides a comprehensive and vivid account of the **Tughlaq dynasty**, administrative practices, and the Sultan's complex personality.
 
• The **Rihla** documents significant historical events, including the **transfer of the capital** from **Delhi to Daulatabad** and the introduction of **token currency** using copper coins.

questions.question: An election to fill a vacancy in the office of President of India occurring by reason of his death, resignation or removal, or otherwise shall be held as soon as possible after, and in no case later than _____ months from, the date of occurrence of the vacancy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 62(2)** of the **Constitution of India**, any vacancy caused by the **death**, **resignation**, or **removal** of the **President** must be filled through an election conducted as soon as possible.
 
• The Constitution mandates a definitive upper limit, stating that such an election must take place no later than **six months** from the date the vacancy occurs.
 
• This provision ensures that the post of the **Head of State**, which is the highest constitutional office in the country, does not remain vacant or be filled by an acting official for an extended duration.
 
• The newly elected **President** does not merely serve the remainder of the predecessor's term but is entitled to hold office for a full term of **five years** as per **Article 56**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Framework for Vacancies**:

 
 
• **Article 65**: Specifies that the **Vice-President** shall act as **President** until a new President is elected and enters upon their office.
 
• **Discharge of Functions**: If the **Vice-President**'s office is also vacant, the **Chief Justice of India** (or the senior-most judge of the **Supreme Court**) performs these duties under the **President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969**.
 
• **Article 62(1)**: Clarifies that an election to fill a vacancy caused by the normal expiration of the term must be completed **before the term expires**.
 
 
 
• **Election Administration**:
 
 
• The **Election Commission of India** (ECI) is the authority responsible for conducting the **Presidential Election**.
 
• The election is held in accordance with the **Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952** and the **Rules of 1974**.
 
• The process involves an **Electoral College** consisting of elected members of both Houses of **Parliament** and the **Legislative Assemblies** of the States.

questions.question: The first successful Indian Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle was _____ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** is a third-generation launch vehicle designed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** to carry **Indian Remote Sensing (IRS)** satellites into **Sun-synchronous orbits**.
 
• The first developmental flight, **PSLV-D1**, was launched on **September 20, 1993**, from **Sriharikota**; however, the mission failed to place the **IRS-1E** satellite in orbit due to a guidance control error.
 
• The mission **PSLV-D2**, conducted on **October 15, 1994**, became the **first successful mission** in the PSLV series by successfully injecting the **IRS-P2** satellite into the desired polar orbit.
 
• The **IRS-P2** satellite weighed approximately **804 kg** and was placed into an orbit at an altitude of **817 km**, proving India's indigenous capability for complex space launches.
 
• This success marked India's transition into the elite group of nations capable of launching satellites into **Polar Sun-Synchronous Orbits**, which are critical for earth observation and resource mapping.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• The second stage utilizes the famous **Vikas engine**, a high-thrust engine developed by **Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC)**.
 
• The vehicle has three main variants: **PSLV-G** (Generic), **PSLV-CA** (Core Alone), and **PSLV-XL**.

• **PSLV-C5**: Launched in **October 2003**, this operational flight successfully placed **IRS-P6 (Resourcesat-1)** into orbit, which was then the most advanced remote sensing satellite.
 
• **PSLV-C7**: Launched in **January 2007**, it was a landmark mission that carried **Cartosat-2** and the **Space Capsule Recovery Experiment (SRE-1)**, demonstrating India's **re-entry technology**.
 
• **PSLV-C15**: Launched in **July 2010**, it carried **Cartosat-2B** along with several international nano-satellites, showcasing the vehicle's versatility in carrying multiple payloads.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Known as the **'Workhorse of ISRO'**, the PSLV has launched iconic missions like **Chandrayaan-1** (2008) and the **Mars Orbiter Mission** (2013).
 
• It holds a world record for launching **104 satellites** in a single mission (**PSLV-C37**) in **2017**.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is NOT correct?

options.text: The states of matter are inter-convertible.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Evaporation causes heating**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement 1 suggests that evaporation results in an increase in temperature; however, in thermodynamics, **evaporation** is essentially a **cooling process**. During this phase change, liquid molecules absorb energy, known as the **latent heat of vaporization**, from their surroundings or the surface they contact, leading to a temperature reduction in that area. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2 describes the **inter-convertibility** of matter. Substances can transition between **solid, liquid, and gas** states through variations in **temperature** and **pressure**, facilitating processes such as **melting**, **freezing**, and **sublimation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Statement 3 classifies **boiling** as a **bulk phenomenon**. When a liquid reaches its **boiling point**, the energy is distributed throughout the entire volume, allowing molecules within the interior to form vapor bubbles and escape. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Statement 4 identifies **evaporation** as a **surface phenomenon**. Unlike boiling, this process occurs only at the interface between the liquid and the air, where molecules with higher **kinetic energy** overcome **intermolecular forces** to escape into the atmosphere. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation**:

 
 
• **Surface Area**: The rate increases with a larger area as more molecules are exposed to the surface.
 
• **Humidity**: A decrease in humidity in the surrounding air increases the rate of evaporation.
 
• **Wind Speed**: Higher wind speeds move vapor particles away quickly, preventing saturation at the surface.
 
 
 
• **Phase Transitions**:
 
 
• **Sublimation**: The direct transition from solid to gas, bypassing the liquid state (e.g., **Camphor** or **Dry Ice**).
 
• **Latent Heat**: The hidden energy required to change the state of a substance without changing its temperature.
 
• **Vapor Pressure**: The pressure exerted by vapor when it is in equilibrium with its liquid phase at a specific temperature.

• **Mediterranean agriculture** is a highly specialized and **capital-intensive** form of **commercial agriculture** practiced in regions surrounding the **Mediterranean Sea**, **California**, central **Chile**, the southwestern part of **South Africa**, and southwestern **Australia**.
 
• The system is uniquely designed to produce high-value crops for the **international market**, making it one of the most profit-oriented agricultural practices globally.
 
• **Viticulture**, or the cultivation of grapes, is the most distinctive specialty of this region; high-quality grapes are used for **wine production**, while others are dried into **raisins** and **currants**.
 
• The region serves as the **orchard of the world**, focusing on the large-scale production of **citrus fruits** (like oranges and lemons), **olives**, and **figs**, which are exported to colder northern climates.
 
• Geographical advantages such as **mild, wet winters** and **hot, dry summers** allow these regions to supply fresh fruits and vegetables to **European** and **North American** markets during the winter season when local production in those areas is impossible.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Typically involves low levels of technology and minimal surplus for **trade** or **market exchange**.

• A primitive practice where land is cleared by **slashing and burning** vegetation.
 
• Farming continues until soil fertility declines, after which the farmer moves to a new plot, known as **Jhumming** in North-East India.
 
 
 
• **Pastoral Farming**:
 
 
• Focuses on the rearing of **livestock** (sheep, goats, cattle) rather than crop production.
 
• Often involves **transhumance**, where herders move animals between seasonal pastures.

BODMAS Rule

questions.question: A square park has sides of length 9 cm. A, 0.5 cm wide path is inside it. What is the area (in square cm) of the path?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **square park** of side **a** with an **inner path** of width **w**:

**Area of path** = 4w(a − w)

Given: side (a) = 9 cm, width (w) = 0.5 cm

Area = 4 × 0.5 × (9 − 0.5) = 2 × 8.5 = 17 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 17 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the **square park** (Outer) = 9 cm

Width of the **path** = 0.5 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f1d17e6a611e3bcd6ad411d002b6906df66eaec8528c14e132f2aef1ea4a2f7.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area of square = (side)²

Area of path = Area of **outer square** − Area of **inner square**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of **outer square** = 9 × 9 = 81 cm²

⇒ Side of the **inner square** = Outer side − (2 × width)

⇒ Inner side = 9 − (2 × 0.5) = 9 − 1 = 8 cm

⇒ Area of **inner square** = 8 × 8 = 64 cm²

⇒ Area of the **path** = 81 − 64 = 17 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 17 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Outer Path Area

When the path is built **outside** the square park, the area is given by 4w(a + w), where 'a' is the side and 'w' is the width.

Cross Path Area

For paths crossing at the center of a rectangle, the area is w(L + B − w), where L is length, B is breadth, and w is path width.

Rectangular Path (Inner)

Area of an **inner path** in a rectangle = 2w(L + B − 2w).

questions.question: ((82.5)² - (69.5)²)/(26) = ?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Algebraic Identity**: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

Here, a = 82.5 and b = 69.5.

Sum = 82.5 + 69.5 = **152**.

Difference = 82.5 − 69.5 = **13**.

Expression becomes: (152 × 13) ÷ 26 = 152 ÷ 2 = **76**.

**∴ The correct answer is 76.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ((82.5)² − (69.5)²) ÷ 26

**Formula Used:** a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)

⇒ ((82.5 + 69.5) × (82.5 − 69.5)) ÷ 26

⇒ (152 × 13) ÷ 26

⇒ 152 × (13 ÷ 26)

⇒ 152 × (1/2)

⇒ 76

**∴ The correct answer is 76.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Two Squares

The identity a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b) is essential for simplifying expressions involving the subtraction of two squared terms without calculating the actual squares.

BODMAS Rule

Always solve operations in the order: Brackets, Orders (powers), Division/Multiplication, and Addition/Subtraction to ensure mathematical accuracy.

Simplification Shortcut

When dividing a product (X × Y) ÷ Z, check if Y is a divisor of Z (or vice versa) to reduce the calculation steps early.

questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 30. Each number is multiplied by C. New average of these 8 numbers is 120. What is the value of C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If each number in a dataset is **multiplied** by a constant **C**, the **Average** of the dataset is also **multiplied** by the same constant **C**.

New Average = Old Average × **C**

120 = 30 × **C**

**C** = 120 ÷ 30 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers (n) = 8

Initial **Average** = 30

New **Average** = 120

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72920daf7a96750a50d58ab4df9d0113b8894d40bbdfc62e08d320d3c3be34f5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Original **Sum** of 8 numbers = Average × Count

⇒ Original **Sum** = 30 × 8 = 240

⇒ When each number is multiplied by **C**, the new sum becomes **C** times the old sum.

⇒ New **Sum** = 120 × 8 = 960

⇒ New **Sum** = Original **Sum** × **C**

⇒ 960 = 240 × **C**

⇒ **C** = 960 ÷ 240

⇒ **C** = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Addition/Subtraction on Average

If a constant **k** is added to or subtracted from every term in a set, the **new average** will be **Old Average ± k**.

Effect of Division on Average

If every number in a set is divided by a non-zero constant **k**, the **new average** becomes **Old Average ÷ k**.

Average Property of Linearity

The **Mean** is a linear operator. For any transformation y = ax + b, the **New Mean** = a × (Old Mean) + b.

questions.question: Average of 35 observations is 52. Average of first 14 observations is 54. Average of last 22 observations is 54. What is the value of 14th observation?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Overall **Average** of 35 observations = 52

Total deviation of first 14 (Avg 54) = 14 × (54 − 52) = +28

Total deviation of last 22 (Avg 54) = 22 × (54 − 52) = +44

Since the 14th observation is **repeated**, its value = Average + Total Deviation = 52 + 28 + 44 = 124

**∴ The correct answer is 124.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total observations = 35 | **Average** = 52

First 14 observations **average** = 54

Last 22 observations **average** = 54

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = **Average** × Number of observations

Value of **overlapping observation** = (Sum of Part 1 + Sum of Part 2) − Total Sum

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/323621aa4736703dfcb2a7541ce6a571c1ff2e73b2d5f3abb92b3b6bcdb91b62.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Sum** of 35 observations = 35 × 52 = 1820

⇒ **Sum** of first 14 observations = 14 × 54 = 756

⇒ **Sum** of last 22 observations = 22 × 54 = 1188

⇒ Total sum of subsets (including 14th twice) = 756 + 1188 = 1944

⇒ Value of 14th observation = 1944 − 1820 = 124

**∴ The correct answer is 124.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Method

In cases of **overlap**, the value of the repeated item is the sum of the base **average** and the net **deviation** of all subsets from that average.

Weighted Average

The combined average of two groups is given by (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and x is the individual average.

Exclusion Case

If a number is **excluded**, the value of the excluded observation = (Old Total Sum) − (New Total Sum).

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 7 : 9 and their Highest Common Factor is 7. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **sum** of two numbers is equal to the **(sum of ratio parts) × HCF**.

Given **ratio** = 7 : 9 and **HCF** = 7.

Sum = (7 + 9) × 7

Sum = 16 × 7 = 112

**∴ The correct answer is 112.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of two numbers = 7 : 9

**Highest Common Factor (HCF)** = 7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10b1cd477fe245cd519b2f7914cf177730189bd5cb127dea0cd68b5ecb7bb767.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 7x and 9x.

⇒ Since 7 and 9 are **co-prime** numbers, their **HCF** is x.

⇒ x = 7 (Given)

⇒ The numbers are (7 × 7) and (9 × 7), which are 49 and 63.

⇒ Sum = 49 + 63

⇒ Sum = 112

**∴ The correct answer is 112.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers A and B, Product of A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B).

LCM in terms of HCF

If two numbers are in ratio a : b and their HCF is x, then their **LCM** = a × b × x.

Difference of Numbers

The difference of two numbers in ratio a : b (where a > b) is given by (a − b) × HCF.

questions.question: 5 kg of water is mixed in 20 kg of milk. What is the percentage of water in the mixture?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Water** : **Milk** = 5 : 20 = 1 : 4.

Total parts in **mixture** = 1 + 4 = 5 units.

**Water percentage** = (Water part ÷ Total parts) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Percentage of component = (Quantity of component ÷ Total quantity) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total weight** of mixture = Weight of milk + Weight of water

⇒ Total weight = 20 kg + 5 kg = 25 kg

⇒ **Percentage of water** = (5 ÷ 25) × 100

⇒ Water % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100

⇒ Water % = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

Percentage Composition

It represents the relative amount of each component in a **mixture** or compound. Sum of percentages of all components always equals 100%.

Mixture Ratios

If component A and B are mixed in ratio x : y, the percentage of A is [x ÷ (x + y)] × 100.

In solutions, concentration is often measured as mass-by-mass percentage: (Mass of solute ÷ Mass of solution) × 100.

questions.question: Total length of train A and train B is 700 metres. These trains are running in opposite direction. Total speed of train A and train B is 70 m/s. In how much time (in seconds) these trains will cross each other?

**Total Distance** = Sum of lengths of Train A and Train B = 700 m.

**Time taken** = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 700 ÷ 70 = 10 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Sum of speeds (VA + VB) = 70 m/s

Direction = **Opposite**

In **opposite direction**, Relative Speed = VA + VB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7c332500369f5fb210b30105648969bd55e32230806a043b91f81302b0e03ca4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = VA + VB = 70 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = LA + LB = 700 m

Crossing Different Objects

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: The speed of stream is 4 km/hr. A boat goes 80 km upstream and comes back to the starting point in 15 hours. What is the speed (in km/hr) of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use **Option Substitution** in the total time equation: Total Time = D / (u − v) + D / (u + v).

Substitute **v = 4**, **D = 80**, and **Total Time = 15**.

Test **u = 12**: 80 / (12 − 4) + 80 / (12 + 4) = 80 / 8 + 80 / 16 = 10 + 5 = 15 hours.

Since the sum matches the given **15 hours**, 12 is the correct value.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of stream (v) = 4 km/hr

Total distance (one way) = 80 km

Total time taken = 15 hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Upstream Speed = u − v | Downstream Speed = u + v (where u is boat speed in still water)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7cde8ad9fdb1b4f75cffb4db8b81b80e5943b1c224e9bc712ad13cf3a8df204b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 80 / (u − 4) + 80 / (u + 4) = 15

⇒ 80 × [(u + 4 + u − 4) / (u² − 16)] = 15

⇒ 80 × [2u / (u² − 16)] = 15

⇒ 160u = 15(u² − 16)

⇒ 32u = 3(u² − 16)

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Will you have finished her portrait before she leaves?

options.text: Has her portrait been finished by you before she left?
Will her portrait have been finished by you before she leaves?
Is the portrait to be finished by you before she leaves?
Will the portrait have finished by you before she left?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will her portrait have been finished by you before she leaves?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is an **Interrogative Sentence** in the **Future Perfect Tense**.

• The structure for the **Active Voice** in this tense is: **Will/Shall + Subject + have + Past Participle (V3) + Object + extension?**

• To convert it into **Passive Voice**, the structure changes to: **Will/Shall + New Subject (Original Object) + have been + Past Participle (V3) + by + New Object (Original Subject) + extension?**

• In this specific case, the original subject is **you**, the verb is **finished**, and the object is **her portrait**.

• During transformation, **her portrait** moves to the subject position, and the agent **you** is placed after the preposition **by**.

• The auxiliary **will have** is transformed into **will have been** to reflect the passive state of a completed future action.

• The time clause **before she leaves** uses the **Simple Present Tense** to refer to a future event; this is a standard grammatical rule and remains unchanged during the voice conversion to preserve the original timeline.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Passive Voice**:

• It is used when the focus is primarily on the **recipient** of the action or the action itself, rather than the person performing it.

• The **Past Participle** form of the main verb is always utilized in passive constructions across all tenses.

• **Future Perfect Tense Specifics**:

• This tense indicates an action that is expected to be **concluded** at a certain point in the future.

• In **Interrogative** forms, the sentence must start with the **auxiliary verb** (Will/Shall) to maintain the questioning tone.

• The inclusion of **been** is mandatory in the passive voice to distinguish it from the active future perfect.

</ul

__

• The **relative pronoun** 'which' refers directly to the **antecedent** **plans**. In English **syntax**, the verb following a relative pronoun must agree in number with its antecedent. Because **plans** is a **plural noun**, the singular auxiliary verb **was** is grammatically incorrect and must be replaced by the plural form **were**.

• The **possessive pronoun** within the clause also refers back to the **plural noun** **plans**. The singular possessive pronoun **its** is only used for singular non-human entities. To maintain **pronoun-antecedent agreement**, the plural possessive **their** must be used to correctly attribute the **long-term consequences** to the multiple plans.

• The original sentence contains a **number disagreement** error where a plural subject is paired with a singular verb and a singular pronoun. The improved phrase **which were formed without taking their potential** rectifies both grammatical inconsistencies.

• By using the plural forms, the sentence logically conveys that each of the **original plans** had potential consequences that were initially overlooked.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Subject-Verb Agreement**:

• This rule dictates that the **verb** must match the **subject** in person and number. For plural nouns like **plans**, **strategies**, or **ideas**, plural verbs such as **were**, **are**, or **have** are required.

• **Pronoun-Antecedent Agreement**:

• An **antecedent** is the noun or pronoun to which a subsequent pronoun refers. 

• **Its**: Used for a singular **neuter** antecedent (e.g., the company, the car).

• **Their**: Used for any **plural** antecedent (e.g., the companies, the cars, the plans).

• **Relative Clauses**:

• A **defining** or **non-defining relative clause** (starting with 'which' or 'that') functions as an adjective. The **grammatical integrity** of the sentence depends on the clause mirroring the properties of the noun it modifies.
